description: We hail from the twin-island Caribbean nation of Trinidad and Tobago—a land of vibrant culture, creativity and innovation. From the birthplace of the steelpan, we carry that same inventive spirit into the stars. Through interactive media, we aim to inspire curiosity, problem-solving and humanity's desire to explore our solar system and beyond. Two islands, looking up with big ideas. Create.Innovate.Explore
summary:
Our project is a Space Mission Design Game inspired by NASA’s Canadarm2 robotic arm wrist-joint replacement mission, conducted on June 30, 2026, during U.S. Spacewalk 95. We developed a mission-based learning concept that allows participants to explore the challenges of planning and carrying out a complex spacewalk to repair critical robotic equipment aboard the International Space Station.

The game incorporates the identification and use of essential EVA tools, astronaut safety equipment, robotic arm components and the sequence of operations required to replace a malfunctioning wrist joint. It also features a realistic mission budget developed through research into NASA information and resources, allowing players to consider costs, resource allocation and financial constraints when planning their mission.

The project makes complex space mission procedures easier to understand through an engaging, interactive experience while introducing participants to space engineering, robotics, teamwork, problem-solving and responsible mission planning.

Although additional missions and subsequent stages of the Canadarm2 mission remain incomplete, we hope that the overall concept, objectives and intended learning experience have been effectively communicated and clearly understood by users.
details:
To reiterate, our project is an interactive Space Mission Design Game inspired by NASA's Canadarm2 robotic arm wrist-joint replacement mission, conducted on June 30, 2026. The game allows players to select a mission, review its summary and identify the necessary replacement components, tools and resources required to complete the repair.

A key feature is its budget management system. Players must make informed decisions when selecting the required parts and equipment. Correct selections contribute towards keeping the mission within its allocated budget, with an interactive 'Within Budget' alert providing feedback. The ultimate objective is to successfully replace the Canadarm2 wrist joint while remaining within budget.

The project is distinctive because it uses real NASA research to introduce players to the equipment, components, procedures and approximate costs associated with an actual space repair mission. It demonstrates how resource allocation, technical accuracy and responsible decision-making can influence mission success and astronaut safety. An incorrect decision could have consequences for the mission and the astronauts carrying out the repairs.

The game was developed using Unity 6 Universal Render Pipeline (URP), Blender for 3D modelling, Paint.NET for visual design and asset editing, and Visual Studio for development.

Although additional missions, the simulated spacewalk and subsequent repair stages remain incomplete due to time constraints, these are areas we hope to develop further.

Beyond education and entertainment, our intended impact is to inspire interest in STEM, aerospace engineering and future space exploration. We also aim to showcase the technological creativity and capabilities of Trinidad and Tobago, demonstrating that talent from a developing nation can contribute meaningfully to global scientific and technological advancements, including future opportunities within NASA and the wider space industry.

Please download the project and run it as needed to play the game.
